Trace stamp of a report

Source: R/trace.R
pub_trace_stamp.Rd

Makes a line that says who made a report, when and with which application, e.g. "Jane Doe at 07-Oct-2026 12:00:00 UTC (myapp v1.2.0)".

Usage

pub_trace_stamp(meta)

Arguments

meta

Document metadata (doc$meta, see pub_doc()) or a document. It must have an author, which pubflow doesn't guess (on a server the system user is the service account).

Value

character(1) trace stamp.

Details

Parts

The stamp consists of

  • the author;

  • the time of the document (time in its metadata, else now) in UTC, with English month names whatever the locale;

  • the application and its version in parentheses. Without app, the parentheses are left out, without version, the version.

The token {trace} in the header and footer lines of a document (see pub_doc()) becomes the trace stamp when the document is rendered to DOCX or PDF. pub_render() adds its meta (e.g. the author of the current session) first.

See also

pub_render(), pub_report_spec()

Examples

meta <- list(author = "Jane Doe", app = "myapp", version = "1.2.0",
             time = as.POSIXct("2026-10-07 12:00:00", tz = "UTC"))
pub_trace_stamp(meta)
#> [1] "Jane Doe at 07-Oct-2026 12:00:00 UTC (myapp v1.2.0)"
pub_trace_stamp(meta[c("author", "time")])
#> [1] "Jane Doe at 07-Oct-2026 12:00:00 UTC"

# In a footer line
doc <- pub_doc(meta = list(footer = c(left = "{trace}")))
